. Though these two poles are simultaneous
becoming, as soon as we examine the way in which
produce and articulate becoming itself, we see that they are a ‘before’ and ‘after’. The difference in nature
– not of degree – between faculty and execution, capacity-to-speak and the spoken word, world and facts, ultimately consists of a radical
that has nothing in common with the empirical succession of two events. The aspect that we must focus on, here, is potential’s role as the

zh: 就时间秩序而言，潜能无条件先于实现。两极虽然在生成变化中同时存在，但只要考察它们如何产生并分节生成变化本身，就会看见二者构成“之前”与“之后”。官能与实行、言说能力与说出的词、世界与事实之间性质而非程度上的差别，最终在于一种根本的历时性；它同两个事件的经验性接续毫无共同之处。这里必须聚焦的，是潜能作为实现之非年代过去所发挥的作用。

en: a) The act is a ‘now’. But what is the structure, and meaning, of this ‘now’? Let us remind ourselves of Émile Benveniste’s observations on the temporal status of an act of speaking.
A concrete utterance always refers (at least implicitly) to the present: but, remember, this is a present that it
establishes through the mere fact of being uttered. The adverb ‘now’ demonstrates the actuality of the discourse that is being voiced; it expresses the time in which it
, unambiguously identifying this with the time in which it
. Like other deictics (‘I’, ‘this’, ‘here’, etc.) the ‘now’ does not refer to any pre-existing reality, but only ‘to the utterance, unique each time, that contains [it]’.
This diagnosis seems straightforward enough, yet it also comprises a point of departure that alters the very notion of
zh: （a）实现是一个“现在”。但这个“现在”具有什么结构和意义？让我们回想埃米尔·本维尼斯特对言说活动之时间地位的观察。
一段具体话语总是至少暗中指向当下；但请记住，这个当下是话语仅凭自己被说出这一事实便自行建立的当下。副词“现在”表明正在发声的话语具有现实性；它表达话语被说出的时间，并毫不含糊地把这个时间认作话语存在的时间。像其他指示词（deictics）——“我”“这个”“这里”等——一样，“现在”并不指向任何预先存在的现实，而只“指向每次都独一无二、包含［它］的那次言说”。
这个诊断看起来相当直接，却也包含一个改变现实性概念本身的出发点。

en: According to Benveniste, the pre-eminent task of terms
such as ‘now’, ‘I’, ‘this’ and ‘here’ is to provide ‘the instrument of a conversion that one could call the conversion of language into discourse’;
deictics guarantee the
from the pure capacity-to-speak (‘before the utterance, language is nothing but the possibility of language’)

to the concrete utterance; they represent the threshold that separates and at the same time correlates the potential and the act. So says Benveniste. But here we must add our own comment. In the case of the deictic ‘now’, the passage from faculty to execution – ‘the conversion of language into discourse’ – exhibits exquisitely
features. That is to say, it means the transition from an indeterminate ‘before’ (language/faculty) to a specific, univocal ‘after’ (discourse/execution). ‘Now’ means:

we have emerged from the non-actuality of potential. The adverb does indicate the unrepeatable moment in which we are speaking, but it indicates it as the moment in which the speaker detaches herself from a past in which there was only ‘the possibility of language’. Since the discourse’s present (or rather, the present that the discourse itself establishes) is the result of a conversion, it thus entails a certain ‘posteriority’.
zh: 本维尼斯特认为，“现在”“我”“这个”和“这里”等词最重要的任务，是提供“一项可以称为把语言转化为话语的转化工具”；
指示词保证从纯粹言说能力——“在言说以前，语言只是语言的可能性”

——过渡到具体话语；它们代表那道既分开又连接潜能与实现的门槛。这是本维尼斯特的说法。但这里必须加上我们自己的评论。就“现在”这个指示词而言，从官能到实行——“把语言转化为话语”——的过程表现出纯粹的时间特征。也就是说，它意味着从一个不确定的“之前”（语言/官能）过渡到一个具体而单义的“之后”（话语/实行）。“现在”的意思是：在我们已经脱离潜能的非现实性以后。这个副词确实指明我们正在言说的不可重复时刻，但它把这一时刻指明为说话者同一段过去相脱离的时刻；在那段过去中，只有“语言的可能性”。话语的当下——更准确地说，话语自身建立的当下——既然是一项转化的结果，便包含某种“在后性”。

en: In general, we tend to consider truly actual only that which comes
a situation in which it was not already present. The most immediate of presences always appears to be a

, standing out from a now-faded ‘back then’. Indulging this intuitive impression, Kant writes: ‘the present, so far as it has come to be, refers us to some preceding state as a correlate of the event which
is given; and though this correlate is, indeed, indeterminate, it none the less stands in a determining relation to the even as its consequence’.

What is all-important, however, is adequately to interpret the ‘after’ that moulds and defines any authentic actuality. Certainly it has nothing to do with a chronological ‘after’. When we say that today’s act is subsequent to yesterday’s act, distinct from it in its date and contents, we bring to light the relation between two presences with different positions
time: but this does not explain what it is that assures both of them (the earlier one no less than the latest one) the rank of
. Indeed, only something which
embodies actuality can be dated ‘before’ or ‘after’ in the calendar. So chronological posteriority presupposes the presence of which it is meant to give account.
zh: 一般而言，我们倾向于只把在某种情境之后才出现、而在该情境中尚未在场的东西，看作真正现实的东西。最直接的在场总显得是一个后果，从一个如今已经褪色的“那时”中凸显。康德顺从这种直观印象，写道：“现在只要是生成的，就使我们回到某个在先状态，把它当作既定事件的对应项；这个对应项固然不确定，却仍然同作为其后果的事件保持规定性关系。”
不过，最重要的是恰当解释那个塑造并界定一切真正现实性的“之后”。它当然与年代性的“之后”无关。当我们说今天的实现后于昨天的实现，在日期和内容上与它不同，我们揭示的是两个在时间中占据不同位置的在场之间的关系；但这并不解释，是什么保证二者——较早者不亚于较晚者——都具有在场地位。事实上，只有已经体现现实性的东西，才能在日历上被标定为“之前”或“之后”。因此，年代性的在后性预设了它原本要说明的在场。

en: This does not mean rejecting the intuitive impression on the basis of which we consider the actual event to be an ‘after something’. Indeed, we ought to recognise a second kind of posteriority that does not belong to the realm of chronology. Not only is the utterance that is currently being spoken subsequent to the utterances that have been spoken hitherto, but it also marks an ‘after’ with respect to the capacity-to-speak. It is wholly at one with ‘now’ precisely because it is previous to that which does

fall in time: dateless potential, an absolute ‘back then’. Moreover, the same goes for utterances spoken in the past: these too, if considered individually, were so many ‘afters’ in relation to the capacity-to-speak.

children: Presence as such is later or subsequent

en: : purely and simply on account of its insertion within becoming, not in terms of a specific position within it. This ‘after’ – which is not at
all relative – appertains to each and every act of whatever date and content, simply because it takes place. The act is
not-now: it takes place

it. If the not-now were a mere logical category (the opposite of actuality), this ‘no longer’ would be a trivial tautology. But it is not. The not-now exhibits the very familiar features of faculties and the world-context: thus it has its own autonomous texture. So, taking obvious license with Kant’s words, we could say: faculties and the world,

, the not-now, are the ‘preceding state’ to which ‘the present refers us … as a correlate of the event which is given’, ‘though this correlate is, indeed, indeterminate’. Except that we ought to specify that the not-now is a ‘previously existing state’ destined to remain
indeterminate.
zh: 这并不意味着拒绝那种使我们把现实事件看成“在某物之后”的直观印象。事实上，我们应当承认第二种不属于年代领域的在后性。当前正在说出的话语不仅后于此前已经说过的话语，而且也标志着相对于言说能力的“之后”。它之所以完全同“现在”一致，恰恰因为它后于某种不落入时间的东西：没有日期的潜能，一个绝对的“那时”。此外，过去说出的话语也一样：如果逐一考察，它们相对于言说能力也都是一个个“之后”。在场本身就是较晚或在后的；理由纯粹而简单，只是它被嵌入生成变化，并不是它在其中占据某个具体位置。这个毫不相对的“之后”属于任何日期和内容的每一项实现，仅仅因为它发生。实现已经不再是非现在：它发生在非现在以后。假如非现在只是一种逻辑范畴——现实性的反面——这个“不再”便只是平庸的同义反复。但它不是。非现在表现出我们极为熟悉的官能和世界—语境之特征，因而具有自身自主的纹理。所以，我们可以对康德的话作出显然超出原意的引申来说：官能和世界，也就是非现在，是“现在使我们回到”的那个“在先状态”，是“既定事件的对应项”；而“这个对应项固然不确定”。只不过还应明确：非现在是一个注定永远保持不确定的“先前存在状态”。

en: This double posterity, characteristic of any given act, is at the origin of numerous

faculty for some identifiable past execution which is attributed the value of a canon or imitable example. Think, moreover, of the mnestic phenomenon of the déjà vu, which we analysed in the first part of the book: she who believes that she is reliving an event that already took place, when in reality she is dealing with something unprecedented, is doing nothing other than dressing potential up in the clothes of a remote – wholly fictitious – actuality which now seems to be repeated even in its slightest details. Awestruck versions of the theory of an ‘eternal return’ even paint the déjà vu in the colours of something truly metaphysical: they postulate the inexorable recurrence of already-spoken words and already-accomplished actions, whereas in fact all that we incessantly ‘return’ to is the capacity-to-speak and capacity-to-do. The

prior act – surreptitiously yet necessarily mashes the characteristics of the chronological ‘back then’ together with those of the potential ‘back then’. It is precisely this usurpatory juxtaposition which explains the
(in the strict Freudian sense) aura and ambiguous sense of authority in which the repeated phenomenon is often clothed.
zh: 任何既定实现所特有的这种双重后继身份，造成了许多张冠李戴。人们经常把过去—潜能还原成一个年代性的过去，把官能误认成某项可以辨认的过去实行，并赋予后者以准则或可供仿效的范例的价值。此外，可以想想本书第一部分分析的既视现象：一个人相信自己正在重新经历已经发生的事件，而实际上面对前所未有之物；她所做的，无非是给潜能披上一件遥远现实性——完全虚构的现实性——的外衣，而这项现实性此刻仿佛正在最细微之处得到重复。怀着惊惧来阐释‘永恒回归’的理论版本，甚至把既视感涂上真正形而上学的色彩：它们设定已经说出的词和已经完成的行动不可避免地重现；但实际上，我们不停“回到”的只有言说能力和行动能力。这个张冠李戴同重复经验——无论真实还是幻觉性的重复——紧密相关：当前重复之实现的原型，即某项可以重复的先前实现，暗中而必然地把年代性的“那时”之特征同潜在的“那时”之特征揉在一起。恰恰是这种篡位式并置，解释了重复现象常常披上的令人不安——严格的弗洛伊德意义上——的光晕和含混权威感。

en: Let us recapitulate. In the temporal

, which is delineated by the relation between potential and act, the traditional primacy of presence falls apart: far from once again taking on the role of barycentre and dividing line of temporality, the ‘now’ is shown to be derivative – or rather,
. The act establishes the category of the present in so far as it comes ‘after’ the faculty and the world-context; it plays a
role, thus

contributing to determining the becoming in which it, too, is absorbed, because it is configured as ‘no longer not-now’. Potential is the past of the act. Yet this is an indefinite past, one that cannot be narrated and has no plot of its own, since it was never itself actual. Potential is not simply anterior, but establishes and holds open the very horizon of anteriority. In the relation between faculty and execution we thus see a disparity (without which it would be impossible even to speak of temporal
, as distinct from chronological
): the act is the empirical ‘after’ of a pure ‘before’. It is, indeed, subsequent to something, but this something is the
. That which falls
time is posterior in relation to time as a unitary whole, as represented – by way of analogy – by the permanent not-now of potential.
zh: 作一总结。在由潜能与实现之间的关系划定的时间秩序中，在场的传统首要地位瓦解了：“现在”远非再次扮演时间性的重心和分界线，反而显得是派生的——更准确地说，是在后的。实现之所以建立当下范畴，是因为它出现在官能和世界—语境“之后”；它发挥使时间化的作用，因而帮助规定那个也把它自身吸收进去的生成变化，是因为它被构成为“不再是非现在”。潜能是实现的过去。然而，这是一个不确定的过去；它无法叙述，也没有自己的情节，因为它自身从未成为现实态。潜能不只是较早，而是建立并保持在先性视域本身的开放。在官能与实行之间的关系中，我们因此看到一种不对等；没有它，甚至不可能把时间秩序同年代推进区分开来。实现是一个纯粹“之前”的经验性“之后”。它确实后于某个东西，但这个东西就是一般过去。落入时间之物相对于作为单一整体的时间是在后的，而时间总体则通过潜能恒久的非现在得到类比性表象。

en: b) We know that Aristotle analysed the potential/act couple from three different angles: in terms of time (τῷ χρονῳ), in terms of being (τῃ ουσιᾳ), and in terms of knowledge (or word: τῷ λογῳ). If we wanted to maintain something of the shape of Aristotle’s exposition – albeit only on the surface – we could say that up until this point we have discussed the priority of potential τῷ χρονῳ, in a directly temporal key, while from now onward we shall privilege the other two paths. Now we will examine this same priority in terms of being (τῃ ουσιᾳ); and subsequently, in terms of knowledge (τῷ λογῳ). Our argumentation concerning ‘what it is’ (being) and how it is to be understood (knowledge) will not, however, leave behind our discussion of temporality. On the contrary, they will be limited to reformulating and delving deeper into this very question. To say τῃ ουσιᾳ and τῷ λογῳ still means to say τῷ χρονῳ, ‘in terms of time’.
zh: （b）我们知道，亚里士多德从三个不同角度分析潜能/实现之对：就时间而言（τῷ χρόνῳ）、就存在而言（τῇ οὐσίᾳ）和就知识——或言说——而言（τῷ λόγῳ）。如果想保留亚里士多德论述的某些外形——哪怕只是表面——可以说，到此为止我们一直以直接的时间方式讨论潜能 τῷ χρόνῳ 的优先；从现在起，将优先选择另外两条道路。我们先就存在（τῇ οὐσίᾳ）考察同一种优先，随后再就知识（τῷ λόγῳ）考察。关于它“是什么”（存在）以及如何得到理解（知识）的论证，并不会抛下时间性问题。恰恰相反，它们只会重述并深化这个问题。说 τῇ οὐσίᾳ 和 τῷ λόγῳ，仍然意味着说 τῷ χρόνῳ，即“就时间而言”。

We also understood, however, that the two simultaneous elements do not co-implicate one another harmoniously, and nor do they remain indifferent to each other: rather, the act

contemporary to the execution, yet only to the execution that challenges and contravenes it. So, given these connections that we know about already, let us pose ourselves the question: what is the essential nature, the ουσια, of potential?
zh: 这里值得再次提到一个已经详细考察过的主题。在年代推进中，潜能与实现始终同时存在。语言官能自身无法标定日期，却因为同一段转瞬即逝的话语发生关系而间接嵌入生成变化；言说活动发生时，这个关系便清楚显现；由此可见，言说能力只有在话语被说出的那个生成时刻，才嵌入生成变化；于是，潜能分享了恰好属于同它相关之实现的日期。不过我们也已明白，两个同时存在的要素既不会和谐地相互蕴含，也不会彼此漠不相关：实现反而否定并存的潜能，使后者遭到遮蔽。官能与实行同时存在，但这实行恰恰挑战并抵触着官能。既然已知这些联系，让我们提出问题：潜能的本质、它的 οὐσία，是什么？

en: In the instant in which the act is accomplished – simultaneous to its accomplishment – the potential is banished. That instant is the present, the ‘now’. But if potential is
banished, then it must previously have existed; but
it was truly itself (because it had still not been negated). Its positive character appears in

negated by the act. That which is currently forbidden can only be named and defined by way of the imperfect tense: we ought to speak of the language faculty or labour-power not in terms of ‘what it is’ but rather

. This does not mean to say that the faculty

past, which is not reducible to chronology because, in conformity with its own essence, it is always
zh: 在实现得到完成的瞬间——与其完成同时——潜能遭到放逐。这个瞬间就是当下，就是“现在”。但如果潜能现在遭到放逐，它此前就必定已经存在；而且在那时，它才真正是它自身，因为它尚未被否定。潜能的肯定性质在回顾中显现：它是一个在被超越的那个时刻，才第一次、也是唯一一次闪烁出来的先前状态。因此，潜能的本质（οὐσία）存在于如今被实现否定的“之前”。此刻被禁止之物，只能用未完成过去时（imperfect）来命名和界定：我们谈论语言官能或劳动力时，不应说它“是什么”，而应说它“曾是什么”。这并不意味着官能曾经作为肯定之物位于过去某个角落，而如今不再存在。恰恰相反，官能自身构成一种独特过去；它不能被还原成年代，因为依照自身本质，它始终是某种曾经如此的东西。

en: The prior state characterised by potential is not at all an enigma. This undateable ‘back then’ corresponds to the condition of
typical of living beings who do not enjoy any pre-given and invariant environment. We have already noted that potential is emblematic of this condition, since it exhibits the

(the not-now or non-actuality) in which the lack of a comforting environmental home initially results. Generic faculties (not to be confused with a finite collection of potential feats) are proof of a lack of specialised instincts and clearly express the

that derives from this. Through a sort of homeopathic process, these faculties oppose the threatening indeterminacy of the world-context with their own indeterminacy or plasticity, thus offering a refuge barely distinguishable from the danger itself. The condition of disorientation and indecision
any historical practice, and thus evades chronological definition: we shall use the term ‘pre-history’ to designate this condition. We will examine

at some length in the third part of this book; nonetheless, it is also worth here sketching out its physiognomy. The essence of potential, its ουσια, is pre-historic: a past that does not belong to any epoch of its own, but rather accompanies each successive actuality. Better, it is a past that we experience only when it is refuted and displaced by the concomitant actuality. The act is a polemical
to the lack of ‘environment’ to which potential
attests. Each act negates the pre-historic indecision and disorientation inherent within the faculty; it is a rebuttal of the sublime ‘before’ in which there
nothing but instability and uncertainty: it poses a temporary remedy to the temporal lacuna (or enduring not-now) that distinguishes existence without an environment.
zh: 以潜能为特征的先前状态毫不神秘。这个无法标定日期的“那时”，对应于那些不享有任何预先给予而恒定环境的生命体所特有的迷失方向处境。我们已经指出，潜能是这种处境的标志，因为它展示了缺少舒适环境家园最初造成的时间缺口——非现在或非现实性。一般官能——不可同有限的潜在本领集合混淆——证明专门本能的缺失，并清楚表达由此产生的犹疑。这些官能通过某种顺势疗法过程，以自身的不确定性或可塑性对抗世界—语境中具有威胁的不确定性，从而提供一个几乎无法同危险本身区分的避难所。迷失方向和犹疑的处境先于任何历史实践，因而逃避年代界定；我们将用“前历史”（pre-history）指称这种处境。本书第三部分会较为详细地考察前历史；但这里也值得先勾勒它的面貌。潜能的本质、它的 οὐσία，属于前历史：这是一个没有自己所属时代、却伴随每一个相继现实性的过去。更准确地说，我们只有在它被同时出现的现实性否定并排挤时，才经验这个过去。实现是针对潜能所证明的“环境”缺失而作出的论战性反应。每项实现都否定官能内在的前历史犹疑和迷失方向；它否定那个只有不稳定和不确定的崇高“之前”，为无环境的存在所特有的时间缺口——或恒久非现在——提供暂时补救。

en: In its essential nature, potential is
. The use of the imperfect tense here inevitably recalls the formula with which Aristotle defines essence in general: τὁ τἰ ἦν εἰναι, that which the being
esse.
The meaning of this expression is a controversial one: for some the ἦν, the ‘was’, appears to mark the causal anteriority of form with respect to matter; others have
understood it as an epistemological expedient allowing Aristotle to establish a thing’s constitutive traits in its pure form,
, that is, taking into consideration the multicoloured mass of accidental and contingent predicates. A great merit of Pierre Aubenque’s

children: Le problème de l’être chez Aristote

en: , is that he instead remains steadfastly loyal to the ‘innocently temporal sense of the imperfect’, that imperfect to which we make recourse in order to indicate ‘a lasting continuity which extends back retroactively before a given event which is assumed as a point of reference’.

Aubenque’s interpretation allows us fully to understand the insurmountable gap which separates the essential nature of potential, which we have just outlined, from Aristotle’s ουσια. Each is at home in the dimension of the past, and the phrase τὁ τἰ ἦν εἰναι pertains to both – but the two are entirely different in terms of the value and field of application they give to the imperfect.
zh: 潜能在其本质中是某种曾经如此的东西。这里使用未完成过去时，不可避免地使人想起亚里士多德用来界定一般本质的公式：τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι，即“存在者曾经是什么”（quod erat esse）。

这句表达的含义颇有争议：一些人认为 ἦν（“曾是”）标志形式相对于质料的因果在先；另一些人把它理解成一种认识论手段，使亚里士多德能够以纯粹形态确定一个事物的构成性特征，也就是在考虑偶然、偶发谓词构成的斑斓总和以前确定它们。皮埃尔·奥邦克《亚里士多德的存在问题》的一项巨大优点，是始终忠于“未完成过去时那种朴素的时间意义”；我们借助这种时态，指明“向后追溯、延伸到某个被当作参照点的既定事件以前的一种持久连续性”。
奥邦克的解释使我们能够充分理解：刚刚勾勒的潜能之本质，同亚里士多德的 οὐσία 之间隔着无法跨越的裂隙。二者都栖居在过去维度，τὸ τί ἦν εἶναι 这一短语也适用于二者；但它们赋予未完成过去时的价值和应用范围完全不同。

en: Aubenque shows that, for Aristotle, the ‘was’ has its origin in
(if we are talking about a living thing) or
(for an inanimate object that moves): demise and stillness are the moments in which a being is distinguished, as its ‘what it was’ now retroactively plays out.
zh: 奥邦克说明，对亚里士多德而言，“曾是”起源于死亡——如果谈论的是生命体——或静止——如果谈论的是运动着的无生命物体：死亡和停止是一个存在者得到区分的时刻，因为它“曾是什么”现在追溯性地展开。

en: Essence pertains to already-concluded biographies, to trajectories that can be recapitulated in light of their conclusion. Only a dead person can be said to be essentially wise: we cannot say this of those who still risk collapsing into stupidity; but we would have to say that the dead person

in essence (ἦν εἰναι) wise. The disclosed past of a potential is, evidently enough, counterposed to the past of a cadaver. After all, the potential’s past is coextensive with any event or action or discourse in life: the ‘was’ is not the archive of a finite series of accomplished acts, but rather appears in concomitance with each single act as it is accomplished, since the act refers back to the not-now which always precedes it. Potential is the unrealised past against which the living measures itself
it lives: faculty, world, pre-history, time as a unitary whole.
zh: 本质属于已经结束的生平，属于那些能够根据结局得到重述的轨迹。只有死者才能被说成本质上是智慧的；仍然面临堕入愚蠢风险的活人不能被如此描述；而对于死者，我们必须说，她本质上（ἦν εἶναι）曾经是智慧的。潜能所揭示的过去，显然同尸体的过去相对立。毕竟，潜能的过去与生命中的任何事件、行动或话语范围相同：“曾是”不是有限系列之已完成实现的档案，而是在每项具体实现得到完成时同它一道显现，因为实现回指始终先于它的非现在。潜能是生命活着时据以衡量自身的未实现过去：官能、世界、前历史、作为单一整体的时间。

en: Death means no longer having such a past,
losing the dateless ‘before’ and having the horizon of anteriority blocked off (the lack of a chronological future is only a corollary or echo of being deprived of the potential past analogous to

). Death thus means reaching a perfect actuality. Aristotle’s ουσια is an imitation of the act of death: the words spoken and the works brought to completion are irrevocably separated from the capacity-to-speak and the capacity-to-do. But the capacity-to-speak and the capacity-to-do are not accidental little wrinkles,

but rather represent the most stable and enduring (that is, least contingent) traits of the living human. So it is only the ‘she was’ uttered during the funeral wake, confirming and commemorating the end of the difference between potential and act, that captures the essence of the dead person. This imperfect adorns the dead person with a certain number of salient memories, and requires in exchange that we forget the other ‘she was’: the substance of the living, characteristic of the non-chronological past within which the capacity-to-speak and capacity-to-do are inscribed.
zh: 死亡意味着不再拥有这样的过去

，失去没有日期的“之前”，使在先性的视域遭到封闭；缺少年代性的未来，只是被剥夺那个类似时间总体的潜能过去所产生的推论或回声。因此，死亡意味着达到完全的现实态。亚里士多德的 οὐσία 模仿死亡这一实现：说出的词和完成的作品不可撤销地同言说能力和行动能力分开。但言说能力与行动能力并非偶然的小皱纹，而是活人最稳定、最持久——也就是最不偶发——的特征。因此，只有守灵时说出的“她曾经是”，才通过确认并纪念潜能与实现差别的终结，把握死者的本质。这个未完成过去时用若干显著记忆装饰死者，并以此为交换，要求我们忘掉另一个“她曾经是”：活人的实体，即以言说能力和行动能力铭写于其中的非年代过去为特征的实体。

en: c) We ought finally to address the anteriority of potential with respect to the act from the cognitive perspective: or, in Aristotelian jargon, its anteriority τῷ λογῳ (in terms of ‘knowledge’, or ‘the word’). How do we become aware of a faculty? With what means can we imagine it and obtain information about its essential nature?
zh: （c）最后，我们应当从认识视角讨论潜能相对于实现的在先性；用亚里士多德的术语，就是潜能 τῷ λόγῳ（就“知识”或“言说”而言）的在先性。我们如何意识到一种官能？借助什么手段才能想象它，并取得关于其本质的信息？

en: Potential is a perpetual not-now. We do not, of course, find anything out about the not-now by way of immediate

: the exclusive object of learning by perception is, indeed, a presence. It might sometimes be believed that the potential not-now dovetails with the future: but if this were so, then to know it would require a
, in the sense of an

. But this would be quite a mistake. I can prefigure and expect the hypothetical actuation of a certain event: i.e., the event itself, in so far as it will become present and perceptible; but I cannot prefigure or expect potential itself, which evades any realisation. Accurate prediction is incongruous with something that even in the future is bound to remain latent and unperceived. So what are we to do? Where direct sensory inquiry and prefigurative reconnaissance fail, we must instead turn to
. We know

that the not-now pertaining to a faculty is contravened and placed between parentheses by the concrete execution that is right now underway. The faculty, which is now negated, existed as such only previously, in an undateable past,
its actual eclipse. The positive essence of the faculty can only be comprehended

, therefore. The mind grasps potential only by way of memory. I grasp an accurate notion of the capacity-to-speak or labour-power when I recall and remember them. The anteriority of potential in terms of knowledge, τῷ λογῳ, does not depend on the fact that we know it before we know of the act (from the chronological perspective, in fact, each of the pair comes into view simultaneously), but rather from the particular
relevant to potential. Potential is memorable, and only memorable, and appears as something previous to the concomitant act, which is instead observed by our perceptive apparatus.
zh: 潜能是永恒的非现在。我们当然不能通过直接知觉认识非现在：知觉学习的唯一对象恰恰是在场。人们有时可能以为潜在的非现在同未来吻合；但如果如此，认识它就要求以期待的方式预先表象它。这完全错误。我能够预先表象并期待某个事件假设性的现实化，也就是事件本身，只要它将会成为在场且可知觉的东西；但我不能预先表象或期待逃避任何实现的潜能本身。对于即使在未来也注定保持潜伏、不可知觉的东西，准确预测毫不相称。那么怎么办？直接感官探询和预先表象的侦察都失败之处，必须转向记忆。我们知道，属于官能的非现在受到此刻正在展开的具体实行的否定，并被放入括号。如今遭到否定的官能，只在此前、在它实际遭遮蔽以前那个没有日期的过去，才作为它本身存在。因此，官能的肯定本质只能回顾性地理解。心灵只能通过记忆把握潜能。当我回想并记住言说能力或劳动力时，才把握关于它们的准确概念。潜能就知识而言——τῷ λόγῳ——的在先性，并非因为我们先于实现而认识潜能——从年代角度看，二者其实同时进入视野——而是源于潜能所要求的特殊认识方式。潜能是可记忆而且只能被记忆的东西；它作为某种先于同时存在之实现的东西出现，后者反而由我们的知觉装置观察。

en: Perception and prefiguration always regard a presence (whether it be real or hypothetical), that is, an act (whether it be current or eventual). Memory, on the contrary, branches in two, and applies to both a former actuality – to definite events which are now far back in time – and the persistent not-now of potential. As it bifurcates, memory gives account of the

past that precedes each and every ‘now’. The memory of an act reproduces the perception we had of it when it took place; it re-presents what was present in a past moment; it allows us to recognise a being or action that we already observed on some other occasion. The memory of potential, conversely, does not hinge on some previous perception: it concerns something (a pure ‘before’, the horizon of anteriority, the past-in-general) that allows
for recollection, since it was never present. To be cognisant of a faculty
is wholly equivalent to recognising it; it is memory that

depicts the capacity-to-speak and labour-power. When memory refers to a potential, it establishes the very notion of that which it is re-evoking: it does operate a reproduction, but, I repeat, this is a

. The retrospective image, far from inferring its object, determines it for itself: it casts aside the distinction between an ‘original’ and a ‘copy’. Since potential exists in the mind only in virtue of memory, it is both the prototype and the replica, the manuscript and the reprint, the sound and the echo.
zh: 知觉和预先表象始终关涉在场——无论现实还是假想的在场——也就是实现——无论当前还是可能的实现。记忆则相反，一分为二，既适用于昔日的现实性——如今远在时间深处的确定事件——也适用于潜能那持续的非现在。记忆在分岔时，说明了先于每一个“现在”的双重过去。对一项实现的记忆，再现了它发生时我们对它的知觉；它重新呈现某个过去时刻曾经在场之物；它使我们能够认出另一个场合已经观察过的存在者或行动。反过来，对潜能的记忆并不以任何先前知觉为枢轴：它关涉某种只能被回忆的东西——纯粹“之前”、在先性视域、一般过去——因为这种东西从未在场。从头认识一种官能，完全等同于认出它；最初描绘言说能力和劳动力的，正是记忆。当记忆指向一种潜能时，它建立自己重新唤起之物的概念本身：它确实进行再现，但必须重申，这是一种生产性的再现（productive reproduction）。回顾的影像并非通过推断获得对象，而是自行规定对象；它抛开“原本”与“摹本”的区别。潜能既然只凭借记忆而存在于心灵中，它便既是原型又是复制品，既是手稿又是再版，既是声音又是回声。

en: How does the mnestic understanding of potential concretely play out? In what circumstances, in ordinary experience, does a
take place? Decisive, here, is memory’s inclination to give the past-form even to events or states of affairs that are

past ones. Indeed, it is precisely in this manner that the dimension of the ‘before’ is liberated from chronological progression, ceasing to be identified with the mass of previous actualities. The phenomenon that attests to this inclination (and characteristically so, not at all as an
exception) is the
: ‘What is duplicating itself at each moment into perception and memory is the totality of what we are seeing, hearing, and experiencing.’

Typical of this phenomenon is the fact that mnestic activity neither presupposes nor retraces perceptive activity, but rather accompanies it perfectly simultaneously, thus affirming itself to be an autonomous mode of understanding. The memory of the present was discussed in great depth in the first part of this book – and now it deserves fresh attention.
zh: 记忆式理解潜能具体如何展开？在日常经验的什么情形中，生产性的再现会发生？这里具有决定意义的，是记忆倾向于把过去形式也赋予并非过去的事件或事态。恰恰以这种方式，“之前”的维度才从年代推进中解放，不再被等同于先前现实性之总和。为这种倾向作证的现象——而且是从特征上作证，绝非作为例外——就是对当下的记忆：“每一时刻被复分为知觉和记忆的，是我们正在看见、听见和经历的一切。”
这一现象的典型之处，是记忆活动既不以知觉活动为前提，也不重循其路径，而是与它完全同时地相伴，从而肯定自身是一种自主理解方式。本书第一部分详细讨论了对当下的记忆；现在，它值得重新关注。

en: It is worth insisting on one aspect, above all else. When we remember the current moment while we are living it, the authentic object of the memory is not, in fact, the present as such, but rather the indefinite (non-chronological) past in which the present is inevitably immersed, merely on account of being remembered. There are thus three – and not two – elements at play, here: a) the perceived present, captured in terms of an act; b) the remembered present, a hybrid intermediate link (since here this same act is taken back to its state of having been possible, the condition of a ‘potential act’); and c) a dateless past, which is exactly the same as the potential. If a) is discourse, c) appears as the language faculty; if the ‘now’ is articulated as pleasure, then the indeterminate ‘before’ consists in the disposition towards enjoyment; and so on. The third element (past-potential), precisely because it is indefinite, requires the second – which, instead, has a precise empirical physiognomy – if it is to see the light of day and be experienced. Though c) appears to be a simple refraction of b), almost as if it were its residue, c) is in fact both the cornerstone and the
result of the whole process. We could even say: c) is the conclusion of a syllogistic inference of which a) and b) are only the premises.
zh: 尤其值得坚持的一点如下。当我们在生活当前时刻之际记住它，记忆的真正对象事实上不是当下本身，而是当下仅仅因为被记住就不可避免地沉入其中的不确定、非年代过去。因此，这里发挥作用的是三个而非两个要素：（a）被知觉的当下，作为实现得到把握；（b）被记住的当下，一个混合的中间环节，因为同一实现被带回其曾经可能的状态，带回“潜在实现”的处境；（c）没有日期的过去，它同潜能完全是同一个东西。如果（a）是话语，（c）就以语言官能显现；如果“现在”被表达成快感，那么不确定的“之前”便由享受禀赋构成；其他情形以此类推。第三个要素——过去—潜能——恰恰因为不确定，需要第二个具有明确经验面貌的要素，才能显露并得到经验。（c）虽然看起来只是（b）的折射，近似于它的残余，事实上却既是整个过程的基石，也是其结果。我们甚至可以说：（c）是一项三段论推理的结论，而（a）和（b）只是前提。

en: A comparison with reminiscence is again useful here. Reminiscence is the mnestic process by which we remember something that we did not know that we knew, since it was initially masked by our forgetting even the fact that we forgot it. Aristotle holds that reminiscence is ‘a certain syllogism’ (

a present image (greater premise) awakens the memory of a past image (lesser premise) which, in turn, through affinity or contrast, hunts for a further, unforeseen object (conclusion): and this is the prey of the struggle to remember. The memory of the present is also a deduction based on three terms; it, too, arrives at a

that could not have been foreseen. However, this apparent similarity masks a radical heterogeneity. The premises of reminiscence are two very different images – after all, they refer to different events. Conversely, the
at work in the memory of the present sets out from a pair of representations (the perceived present and the remembered present) which are wholly

in their factual content: both a) and b) hinge on what we are seeing, hearing and experiencing right now. The only distinction between these premises is their temporal index: the remembered present, the middle term of the inference, is inscribed in a pure or formal ‘back then’, which is extraneous to the calendar. The double consideration of one same
does not lead to the recuperation of another state of affairs which had until then been forgotten (as in the case of
reminiscence, conversely). The conclusion of this syllogism instead concerns the

that alone is able to distinguish between two premises which are otherwise the same. That is to say, it concerns the non-chronological past in which the current moment is transposed. This past is the original and unforeseen
of a peculiar mnestic
zh: 这里再次适合拿回忆（reminiscence）来作比较。回忆是一种记忆过程：我们记起某种自己并不知道自己知道的东西，因为起初，连自己曾忘记它这件事也一并忘了，这就把它遮蔽起来。亚里士多德认为，回忆是‘某种三段论’（syllogismos tis）：

一个当下的影像（大前提）唤醒对某个过去影像（小前提）的记忆；后者又通过相似或对照，追索另一个未曾预见的对象（结论），而这个对象就是努力回忆所捕获的猎物。对当下的记忆同样是一种建立在三项之上的推演，也同样抵达一个无法预见的对象。然而，这一表面相似掩盖着根本的异质性。回忆的前提是两个截然不同的影像——毕竟，它们指向不同的事件。相反，在对当下的记忆中起作用的 syllogismos tis，从一对事实内容完全相同的表象出发，即被知觉的当下和被记住的当下：（a）与（b）都围绕我们此刻正在看见、听见和经历的东西。两个前提之间唯一的区别，是它们的时间标记：作为推论中项的被记住之当下，被铭写在一个纯粹或形式的‘那时’之中，而这个‘那时’处于历法之外。对同一个此时此地（hic et nunc）的双重考察，并不会像回忆那样，重新取得另一个此前遭到遗忘的事态。这个三段论的结论所涉及的，反而是唯一能够区分两个其余方面完全相同的前提的时间差异。也就是说，它涉及当前时刻被移置进去的那个非年代过去。这个过去，是一种独特的记忆性再现所产生的原初而未曾预见的产物。

en: Every self-reference hinges on the relation between act and potential. The formulas ‘language which speaks of language’ and ‘thought that thinks about itself’ mean: an act of speech which gives account of the capacity-to-speak, and an act of reflection which refers back to the faculty of reflection. Every self-reference has a temporal structure and re-evocative tonality. Indeed, it involves a diachrony, linking the act’s ‘now’ to the potential’s indeterminate ‘already back then’.

children: Every self-reference is a memory of the present

en: . As we have just seen, when we remember the instant that is currently underway, we are remembering the faculty correlated to the act that is being executed: for example, the faculty of thinking, if the current instant is characterised by an act of meditation. Every self-reference that is brought to a successful conclusion (and not caught up in vicious circles) is always indirect, mediated by memory; it is fulfilled through a retrospective gaze on the
; it has the form of a
syllogism whose conclusion is not a state of affairs, but rather the past in general.
zh: 一切自指（self-reference）都取决于实现与潜能的关系。‘谈论语言的语言’和‘思考自身的思想’这些公式意味着：一种说明言说能力的言说行动，以及一种回指反思官能的反思行动。一切自指都具有时间结构和重现的调性。事实上，它包含一种历时性，把行动的‘现在’同潜能那不确定的‘早在那时’联结起来。一切自指都是对当下的记忆。正如我们刚才看到的，当我们记住当前正在展开的瞬间时，我们所记住的是与正在实行的行动相关联的官能；例如，如果当前瞬间由沉思行动来刻画，那么我们记住的便是思考官能。每一种成功完成、未陷入恶性循环的自指总是间接的，并以记忆为中介；它通过回顾此时此地而完成；它采取一种独特三段论的形式，其结论不是某个事态，而是一般过去。

en: . Whenever the memory of the present is not lived as such, but instead gives rise to the pathological feeling of déjà vu, self-reference is perverted and transformed into

the original act from who-knows-what date that the current moment seems to be perfectly faithfully repeating. The language faculty, for example, is fetishistically reduced to one or several utterances prior to the current one. The regression to the infinite is provoked by the attempt to grasp the archetypal act that is now apparently being retraced. I utter a phrase: I have a cat; then I create its meta-linguistic double in quotation marks, ‘I have a cat’, thus intending to demonstrate the model at the basis of the phrase in question. But this model is an evasive one. The first level of meta-language presupposes another, more comprehensive one (“I have a cat”), in turn referring to a third level (“ ‘I have a cat” ’), and so on, in an interminable search looking ever further backward. It is interminable because the thing that we are constantly pursuing is not one original act of speech, but rather the capacity-to-speak pure and simple (which is not commensurable to any determinate act of speech, however old or recent, real or possible). The regression to the infinite is nothing but the dynamic image – whether mercurial or feverish – of that same aporia which, in the déjà vu phenomenon, instead seems to have been petrified.
zh: 释论。每当对当下的记忆没有被作为这种记忆来体验，反而引发既视感（déjà vu）的病理感觉时，自指便遭到扭曲并转化为无穷倒退。我们已经知道，在既视现象中，潜能虚假地表现为一次先前实现，表现为不知发生于何日的原初行动，而当前时刻似乎正无比忠实地重复它。比如，语言官能被拜物教式地还原为当前话语之前的一句或数句话。试图把握眼下似乎正在被重走的原型行动，由此引发无穷倒退。我说出一句话：我有一只猫；然后给它制造一个加上引号的元语言复本——‘我有一只猫’——意在借此展示作为该句话基础的模型。但这个模型不断逃逸。元语言的第一层预设了另一个更具包容性的层次（在‘我有一只猫’之外再加一层引号），后者又指向第三层（在已经带有双层引号的表达之外再加一层引号），如此等等，在不断向后搜寻中没有尽头。之所以没有尽头，是因为我们不断追逐的并非某个原初言说行动，而是纯粹的言说能力；它同任何确定的言说行动都不可通约，不论那一行动古老还是新近、现实还是可能。无穷倒退不过是同一个疑难的动态影像——或变幻不定，或狂热不安；而在既视现象中，这个疑难仿佛凝固成石。

zh: 至少有两个充分理由，可以把元潜能这一角色归于记忆。第一个十分清楚：正是这种官能，使我们能够经验其他一切官能，也能经验作为无定形可感语境的世界。记忆能力，是理解潜在非现在借以表达自身的各种形态之可能性条件。第二个理由同样重要，却更为曲折，需要我们先陈述它的前提。记忆本身也是经验和理解的对象。像任何态度或禀赋一样，记忆同样是一种知觉无法触及的非现在。总之，记忆本身也通过记忆性的再认——更准确地说，通过生产性的再现——而得到认识。我们不仅拥有对言说能力或劳动力的记忆，也拥有对记忆能力的记忆。事实上，我们有理由相信，后者是一切后续潜能重现的基础与框架。那么，如果我们把记忆能力看成我们所（再）认识的东西，而非知识的源泉，它的独特之处究竟是什么？

zh: 当记忆自身被对象化并得到阐明时，它配得上元潜能之名，因为它构成一个属，而其他官能则是这个属的种。言说能力和劳动力只能以局部而有缺陷的方式，例示构成潜能的非年代过去。它们各自的规定内容——分别是能言性和制作（poiesis）——实际上并不直接具有时间性。它们是一个没有日期的‘那时’，但这个‘那时’只是隐含地存在，被灌注在某种混入其中的异质要素之内，又被该要素遮蔽。相反，记忆能力唯一的内容就是在先性维度，就是‘那时’本身。因此，记忆使我们能够看见一切官能共有的时间基底；它体现非年代过去这个属，而其他官能只是这一属的具体例证或具体化形式；它还预示一种尚未得到分节、尚无自身名称的潜能。

en: In his

(Books X and XIV) Augustine sees a fundamental analogy between the faculties of the mind and the personas of the Holy Trinity. Memory is the image of the Father, the intellect imitates the Son, and will corresponds to the Holy Spirit. And yet the Father, though only one of the three figures, also alone comprises
the whole Trinity.
In the same way, memory, though representing a single prerogative of the mind, also coincides with the mind in general. Part and whole, both at

once, it is the attitude underlying any other attitude. The proof is the manner in which self-reflection takes place. Being cognisant of itself, the mind confirms its capacity-to-remember, capacity-to-think and capacity-to-will. But the mind – finding nothing strange or unusual within the mind – is only cognisant of itself in a single guise: re-cognising itself in virtue of a mnestic performance.
It is a memory, therefore, that generates its understanding of the capacity-to-remember, the capacity-to-think and the capacity-to-will. Moreover: the mind as a whole not only always
a memory of itself, but it

this memory, this capacity to re-call itself or to re-cognise itself. As such, the various faculties understood thanks to memory, are also a specification or an offshoot of memory. The capacity-to-remember is the

zh: 奥古斯丁在《论三位一体》（De Trinitate）第十卷和第十四卷中，看到心灵诸官能与神圣三位一体诸位格之间的一种根本类比。记忆是圣父的形象，智力效仿圣子，意志则对应圣灵。然而，圣父虽只是三个位格之一，却又独自包含整个三位一体。
同样，记忆虽然代表心灵的一种特有能力，却也同一般心灵重合。它同时既是部分也是整体，是一切其他态度赖以成立的态度。自我反思发生的方式便是证明。心灵认识自身时，确认自己的记忆能力、思考能力和意志能力。但心灵——在心灵内部没有发现任何陌生或异常之物——只以一种形态认识自身：凭借记忆活动再认自身。
因而，正是记忆产生了心灵对记忆能力、思考能力和意志能力的理解。不仅如此：作为整体的心灵不仅始终拥有对自身的记忆，而且它就是这种记忆，就是这种重新唤回或再认自身的能力。因此，借助记忆而得到理解的各种官能，同时也是记忆的特殊化或分支。记忆能力就是拥有诸官能的官能，这句话有双重含义：它既是通向多种具体态度的认识路径，也是这种多样性的属或统一基底。这双重含义，对应于我们刚才考察的元潜能概念的双重意义。

en: But someone will say, that is not memory by which the mind, which is ever present to itself, is affirmed to

remember itself; for memory is of things past, not of things present … But let anyone who denies that there is any memory of things present, attend to the language used even in profane literature, where exactness of words was more looked for than truth of things. ‘Nor did Ulysses suffer such things, nor did the Ithacan forget himself in so great a peril.’ For when Virgil said that Ulysses did not forget himself, what else did he mean, except that he remembered himself? And since he was present to himself, he could not possibly remember himself, unless memory pertained to things present. And, therefore, as that is called memory in things past which makes it possible to recall and remember them; so in a thing present, as the mind is to itself, that is not unreasonably to be called memory, which makes the mind at hand to itself.
zh: 然而有人会说，心灵始终对自身在场，所以所谓心灵记得自身，凭借的并不是记忆；因为记忆属于过去之物，而不属于当下之物……但凡否认当下之物也有记忆的人，请留意世俗文学中的遣词；在那里，人们更看重用词的精确，而非事物的真理。‘尤利西斯没有承受这样的事情；伊萨卡人在如此巨大的危险中也没有忘记自己。’维吉尔说尤利西斯没有忘记自己，除了说他记得自己，还能是什么意思？既然他对自己在场，他若不是对当下之物也有记忆，就绝不可能记得自己。因此，正如对过去之物而言，那种使我们能够回想并记住它们的能力被称作记忆；对于当下之物——例如心灵之于自身——而言，那种使心灵呈现于自身面前的能力，被称作记忆也并非没有道理。

We know that Hegel drew a useful connection between essence and the past, thus re-evoking Artistotle’s τὁ τἰ ἦν εἰναι: ‘The German language has preserved essence [Wesen] in the past participle [gewesen] of the verb to be; for essence is past – but timelessly past – being’ (G.W.F. Hegel,

(New York: Columbia University Press 1942, p. 148) he writes: ‘But if a present cannot be conceived which does not rest on a past, then also no eternal present can be conceived which is not grounded in an eternal past.’ A little further on (pp. 150–1) he writes: ‘An eternal being conscious cannot be conceived, or it would be like unconsciousness There is no becoming conscious (and therefore no consciousness either) without positing something as past … all consciousness has what is unconscious as ground, and, just in coming to be conscious, this unconscious is posited as past by that which becomes conscious of itself. Now it is certainly not conceivable that God has been unconscious for a long time and then become conscious. But it is quite conceivable that the unconscious and conscious in God were comprehended in the same indivisible act of becoming conscious, the conscious as what is eternally present, but the unconscious with the character of what is eternally past.’

zh: ‘正是苏格拉底之死塑造了苏格拉底的本质：一位遭到不公正定罪的正义者。正是他的死亡，使我们能够把苏格拉底历史存在中的偶然因素和他生活中的偶发方面，同那些本质上属于苏格拉底的属性之尊严分离开来。一个人的本质，是他从历史到传说、从悲剧性的——因为未曾预见——生存到已经完成之命运的转化；而这种转化只有通过死亡才会发生。用更抽象的话说，用于一个人的未完成过去时（imperfect）——所指的是因已不复存在而不在之物——并不影响对他的本质属性的判定（至少，如果我们在严格归属而非仅仅一般归类的意义上理解这一点）。’（同上，第469页）
en: ‘It was the death of Socrates that shaped the essence of Socrates: that of the unjustly condemned just man. It is his death that allows us to dissociate the contingencies of Socrates’ historical existence and the accidental aspects of his life from the dignity of his essentially Socratic attributes. The essence of a man is his transfiguration from history into legend, from a tragic – because unforeseen – existence into a destiny fulfilled: and this transfiguration only takes place through death. In more abstract terms, what is imperfect about a man – concerning what is not because it is no longer – does not weigh on his essential attributes (if, at least, we understand this to mean an attribution properly speaking, not just in generic terms)’ (Ibid., p. 469).

zh: 从亚里士多德 οὐσία 的立场看，死者是没有未来的人；但从潜能的视角看，死者却是不可撤销地失去一般过去、‘那时’维度和 ἦν 的人。宗教对死后状态的关注、由奖赏或痛苦组成的‘彼岸’表象，并不标志着对未来的渴望——不惜一切也要拥有未来的愿望——而是保存我们自己的非年代过去、保存自身潜能的冲动。
en: From the standpoint of Aristotle’s ουσια, a dead man is he who has no future; from the viewpoint of potential, however, the dead man is he who has irrevocably lost the past-in-general, the dimension of the ‘back then’, the ἦν. The religious interest in our post-death status, the representation of a ‘beyond’ composed of gratification or suffering, does not signal a yearning for the future, the desire to have a future despite everything, but the impulse to conserve our own non-chronological past, our own potential.

zh: 请考虑克尔凯郭尔的观察：‘重复与回忆是同一种运动，只是方向相反；因为被回忆之物已经存在，是向后重复，而真正的重复则是向前回忆。’（索伦·克尔凯郭尔，《恐惧与战栗／重复》，普林斯顿：普林斯顿大学出版社，1983年，第131页）重复是一种操作性的记忆，它借此恢复过去之物；记忆则是一种无形体的重复，它借此用影像取代过去之物。因此，在生产性的再现中，先前事物与记忆影像之间的一切区别都消散了。就潜能而言，回到某物（回忆）与某物的复归（实践性重演）完全吻合。生产性的再现既是‘向后重复’，也是‘向前回忆’。
en: Consider Kierkegaard’s observation that ‘Repetition and recollection are the same movement, except in opposite directions, for what is recollected has been, is repeated backward, whereas genuine repetition is recollected forward’ (Søren Kierkegaard,
, Princeton: Princeton University Press 1983, p. 131). Repetition is an operative memory, through which it restores the past
; memory is a bodiless repetition, through which it replaces the past thing with its
. So in the

, all distinction between the previous thing and the mnestic image evaporates. As concerns potential, the return-to (recollection) and return-of (practical reiteration) match flawlessly. The productive reproduction is as much ‘repeated backward’ as it is ‘recollected forward’.

zh: 奥古斯丁，《论三位一体》X, 11, 18，ccel.org：‘记忆、理解和意志这三者，并非三种生命，而是一种生命；也非三个心灵，而是一个心灵；因而它们当然也不是三种实体，而是一种实体……就它们各自而言，无论还分别用什么名称来称呼，它们合在一起时也不是以复数而是以单数来称呼。但就它们彼此相互关联而言，它们是三；如果它们并不相等——不只各自彼此相等，而且每一个都同全体相等——它们当然无法彼此包含；因为不仅每一个包含于另一个之中，而且全体也包含于每一个之中。因为我记得自己拥有记忆、理解和意志；我理解自己在理解、意愿和记忆；我意愿自己在意愿、记忆和理解。’这些官能在实体上同一，却因各自同另外两项发生关系的方式不同而有区别，从而为三位一体提供一个洞见深刻的形象。不过奥古斯丁在第十四卷中指出，心灵往往并不以明确方式认识自己，因此不知道或忘记自己就是记忆、理智和意志。那么，心灵与神圣位格之间的类比是否由此瓦解？完全没有。奥古斯丁回答说，因为无论如何，心灵仍保留对心灵的隐含觉知：一种无意识、先行且不变的记忆，其中包含官能充分分节的种子。心灵‘在没有构想自身时，似乎确实不在自己的视线中，也没有从自身形成对自身的知觉；但它仍然认识自身，仿佛它对自身而言就是一份关于自身的记忆’（XIV, 6, 8）。因此，记忆—圣父隐含地预示整个三位一体：‘我们必须考察，理解（intellectus）以何种方式属于构想，而心灵中每个事物的认识（notitia），即使人在没有思考它时，也被说成只属于记忆。因为如果确实如此，那么心灵原本并不拥有这三项，即对自身的记忆、理解与爱〔也就是意志〕；它只是记得自身，后来开始思考自身时，才理解并爱自身’（XIV, 7, 9）。又说：‘如果我们转向心灵的内在记忆——它借此记得自身，转向内在理解——它借此理解自身，也转向内在意志——它借此爱自身；这三者始终共存，并且从它们开始存在起便始终共存，无论是否正在被思考，那么这个三位一体的形象确实会显得甚至只属于记忆’（XIV, 7, 10）。

: ‘[T]hese three, memory, understanding, will, are not three lives, but one life; nor three minds, but one mind; it follows certainly that neither are they three substances, but one substance … whatever else they are severally called in respect to themselves, they are called also together, not plurally, but in the singular number. But they are three, in that wherein they are mutually referred to each other; and if they were not equal, and this not only each to each, but also each to all, they certainly could not mutually contain each other; for not only is each contained by each, but also all by each. For I remember that I have memory and understanding, and will; and I understand that I understand, and will, and remember; and I will that I will, and remember, and understand.’ Identical in substance but distinct in terms of the way in which they enter into relation with the other two, these faculties offer a perspicacious image of the Trinity. Nonetheless, Augustine observes in Book XIV, often the mind does not know itself in an explicit manner and thus ignores or forgets that it is memory, intelligence and will. But does the analogy between the mind and the personas of the divine thus fall apart? Not at all, Augustine responds, because in any case the mind still retains an

of the mind: a sort of unconscious, preliminary and invariant memory that contains the seed of the faculty’s full articulation. The mind, ‘when it is not conceiving of itself, it appears that it is not indeed in its own sight, nor is its own perception formed from it, but yet that it knows itself as though it were to itself a remembrance of itself’ (XIV, 6, 8). For this reason, the memory-Father
anticipates the Trinity as a whole: ‘we must inquire in what way understanding (
) belongs to conception, while the notion (
) of each thing that is in the mind, even when one is not thinking of it, is said to belong only to the memory. For if this is so, then the mind had not these three things:

. the remembrance, the understanding, and the love of itself [that is, will]; but it only remembered itself, and afterwards, when it began to think of itself, then it understood and loved itself’ (XIV, 7, 9). And again: ‘if we refer ourselves to the inner memory of the mind by which it remembers itself, and to the inner understanding by which it understands itself, and to the inner will by which it loves itself, where these three always are together, and always have been together since they began to be at all, whether they were being thought of or not; the image of this trinity will indeed appear to pertain even to the memory alone’ (XIV, 7, 10).
